Subject: Everly - throughput & capacity assumptions for dedicated commit

Hi Alice / Everly team,

Following up on our call — attaching a simple model so we can line up on committed capacity. We need 3 things confirmed from your side to finalize the Dedicated proposal:

1) Typical request size (avg tokens per call) and distribution (p50/p90/p99).
2) Peak QPS (or concurrent requests) during your busiest 10-minute windows.
3) Target latency SLO (p95 end-to-end for a 512-token generation, or per-token streaming target).

Our initial assumptions for modeling (attached workbook):
- Model family: Llama2-13B (8-bit/4-bit quantized variants). We also include a smaller Mistral-lite option for comparison.
- Measured throughput (approx): A10G: 600 tokens/sec (q4_0 13B), H100: 2200 tokens/sec (q4_0 13B). These are steady-state single-stream numbers at batch sizes optimized for low-latency.
- Latency SLO used for sizing: p95 <= 550ms for typical 256-token responses (streaming enabled), with a headroom multiplier of 1.5 for bursts.

Attached: everly_workload_samples.csv, initial_capacity_model.xlsx

If you can reply with the numbers above I’ll convert to concrete GPU quantities and two commit options (conservative H100 pool and cost-optimized A10G pool) and include cost delta and rollback/canary plan.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Manager | Redwood Inference

Thanks Neha — good summary. Quick answers below and a couple of clarifying questions: 

- Avg tokens per call: 180 (p50 140 / p90 420 / p99 900). We have a mixed profile: ~15% of calls are long-form (>512 tokens) and 70% are short (<200 tokens).
- Peak QPS: Our busiest 10-minute window historically maps to ~120 requests/sec (we measure at the API gateway).
- Target SLO: p95 end-to-end generation latency <= 600ms for responses up to 256 tokens; for long-form (>512 tokens) we can tolerate p95 <= 2.5s as long as streaming progress is steady.

A couple of asks: can you show the GPU math for both A10G and H100 (we want cost vs risk tradeoffs) and indicate any required commit length for pricing. Also, our procurement team wants a canary approach so we can start smaller (8 GPUs) and scale to target over 4 weeks.

--

Thanks for the numbers, Alice — did the quick math and sketched two options. Sharing the calc here (quick notes):

Assumptions:
- Peak QPS = 120 req/s
- Avg tokens = 180 tokens/req
- Peak tokens/sec = 120 * 180 = 21,600 tokens/sec

Measured throughput (per single GPU, low-latency config):
- A10G (13B q4): ~600 tokens/sec
- H100 (13B q4): ~2200 tokens/sec

Base GPU counts (steady-state) = ceil(21,600 / tokens_per_gpu):
- A10G: 21,600 / 600 = 36 -> 36 GPUs
- H100: 21,600 / 2200 = 9.82 -> 10 GPUs

Apply operational headroom multiplier (x1.5 recommended for bursts, rolling upgrades, cache misses):
- A10G w/headroom: 36 * 1.5 = 54 GPUs
- H100 w/headroom: 10 * 1.5 = 15 GPUs

Canary path (Alice request): start with 8 H100-equivalent GPUs (or 30 A10G-equivalent) and scale to target over 4 weeks. Note: elasticity w/auto-burst can reduce initial commit liability but procurement typically prefers predictability.

Notes on latency/SLO fit:
- With A10G at these batch sizes we often see slightly higher tail latency for long-form jobs; must rely on caching and routing to reduce p95.
- H100 provides strong margin on p95 for both short and long responses and lowers the chance of degraded p95 under bursts.

Next steps: I’ll pack this into two commercial options (16H100 commit vs 60A10G commit) with pricing and a canary/add-on delta. Neha, want to confirm which of these we price as the default commit for the deal.

--

Thanks Marcus — that's very helpful. We scoped this with finance and procurement: two follow-ups from our side before final commit:

1) We prefer H100s for the first commit given latency sensitivity and lower ops risk. Suggested starting point: commit to 16 H100s, with the canary path to start at 8 and scale to 16 in 2–3 weeks. If our usage grows faster we'll bump to 24.
2) Procurement requests a one-page canary/runbook and a DocuSign term sheet outlining the commit and early-termination conditions.

If Redwood can prepare the term sheet + canary plan and a short note on rollback (how we fail over to hosted models or lower-cost variants) we can route for signatures this week. Also include the HubSpot deal id EV-2026-0142 in paperwork so procurement maps the discount.
